substantive_reconstruction.vanishing_kernel: Let A=(x+1)^(k+1), B=x^(k+1), E=AB, with k>=0. E is monic of degree 2k+2. At -1 the A factor supplies a zero of multiplicity at least k+1, and at 0 the B factor does so, hence all derivatives of orders 0 through k vanish at both nodes. Conversely, if a polynomial h has these zero jets, its Taylor coefficients at each node through order k vanish because h^(j)(a)=j! times that Taylor coefficient and j! is nonzero over R. Thus A divides h and B divides h. The distinct linear factors are coprime, so their powers are coprime and E divides h. This proves equality of the zero-jet kernel with E R[x], including the converse needed for the full solution set.
substantive_reconstruction.nonempty_affine_fiber: For prescribed real derivative values u_j at -1 and v_j at 0, the local Taylor polynomials sum_{j=0}^k u_j(x+1)^j/j! and sum_{j=0}^k v_j x^j/j! realize the two local jets. Coprimality gives a Chinese-remainder polynomial with those residues modulo A and B. Taking its remainder modulo E leaves both residues unchanged and yields a representative p0 of degree less than 2k+2, hence at most 2k+1. This constructs a solution for arbitrary real data, not just the source's exp(-1),(-1)^j special data. Every other solution p satisfies E divides p-p0, so the complete set is exactly p0+E R[x]. It is a vector subspace exactly when all prescribed jets vanish, because only then does it contain zero.
substantive_reconstruction.unrestricted_affine_dimension: Multiplication by E is an injective R-linear map R[x] onto E R[x]: if E q=0 then q=0 since R[x] is an integral domain and E is nonzero. The images of the standard monomial basis are E x^m for m in N. Every polynomial multiplier has finite monomial support, so this family spans the translation space. For any finite linear combination sum_m c_m E x^m=0, canceling nonzero E gives the zero polynomial sum_m c_m x^m, forcing every c_m=0. The family is therefore a countably infinite Hamel basis. The affine dimension is aleph_0 over R; the uncountability of R or of the affine set itself does not change this algebraic dimension. The answer correctly avoids substituting either a finite dimension or the cardinality of the coefficient set.
substantive_reconstruction.capped_slices_and_sharpness: For d>=0 and the cap 2k+1+d, a nonzero multiplier q satisfies deg(E q)=2k+2+deg(q). Because deg(p0)<=2k+1, its leading term cannot cancel that of nonzero E q. Thus deg(p0+E q)<=2k+1+d exactly when deg(q)<=d-1, while q=0 is always allowed. Equivalently the multipliers are the span of 1,x,...,x^(d-1), interpreted as the zero space when d=0. These slices have affine dimension d. In particular degree<=2k+1 admits only p0 and the next degree admits the new direction E. The unrestricted fiber is not any one of these finite slices, although it is their increasing union. For k=0 this reduces to E=x(x+1), a unique affine-linear interpolant plus arbitrary multiples of E, so the smallest-order boundary case also works. All-zero jets give p0=0 and the same dimension reasoning without an artificial nonzero-polynomial degree assumption.
